title: Audit PR256’s complex program against its pinned Lean proof (no new κ)
body:
PR256's explicit complex program and the corresponding Fourier Lean proof live in separate repositories. This adds a self-contained audit that checks their agreement and retains a separate reproduction of the pinned proof. **No new κ, network, or Fourier exponent is claimed.**

The contribution lives in `research/pr256-fourier-audit/` and adds:

- Exact program, five-stage histogram, rational moment and finite-fill checks, plus agreement with the Lean input and exponent literals.
- Immutable source pins, a source-only proof archive, source-origin ledgers, and the original build/regeneration receipts with compressed logs.
- A Lean reproduction command, eleven audit controls (two positive and nine negative), and a Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 finite-audit workflow.
- An explicit dependency table distinguishing the formal exact-complex WHT/DFT result from the bit-side and implementation obligations still needed for multiplication.

The program is pinned to PR #256 at `db3f75cdc5f03f3131d48fb220f6bf1958404ff3`; the proof is pinned to [wht-power-saving-lean PR #2](https://github.com/jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean/pull/2) at `fd19e46b728faa414cbfbf91b01a6a0b7903375d`. This package can be reviewed before #256 merges. It leaves existing witnesses, selected-result pointers, and source files unchanged.

Credit belongs to Jacob Sussman for the formal framework and checker, Chafik Boukhalfa for the explicit program and stronger instantiation, and the underlying OpenAI/community construction. Original notices are preserved; the added notice credits OpenAI, Doug Colkitt, Rohan Arun, Swapnil Jain, and the other construction contributors. Ryan Shea contributes this separate reproduction and consistency audit, adapted from [the pinned downstream project](https://github.com/shea256/fourier-transform-below-nlogn/tree/a101b363b38e6bf7d309042c94ba5fa18a424fad), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

### Validation

- Offline audit and all eleven controls pass locally on Python 3.11, 3.13 and 3.14.
- The [new audit workflow passed on Ubuntu for all three Python versions](https://github.com/shea256/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38023387048).
- Separate checkout comparisons match all 20 PR256 package files and 456 proof-source files. All 91 OpenAI origin files were fetched again from the pinned revision and match.
- The retained historical fresh project build passed using the pinned Mathlib cache. The ported wrapper was also rerun successfully against that existing build: both generators, staged scalar targets, combined build, axiom check, and WHT/Fourier comparisons passed. That wrapper rerun is not described as another fresh build.
- `make entrance-bank-verify` passes.
- The [broader Linux regression workflow passed all 52 jobs](https://github.com/shea256/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38023387071), including every `make verify` group on Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 and the existing formal packages. The local macOS `make verify` run stopped at the unchanged skip-suffix producer because Apple clang rejects `-fopenmp`; this platform limitation was not changed as part of the audit. The committed validation note records the earlier submission-time status; these CI results are the completed follow-up.

Receipt validation does not rerun Lean. The new CI runs the finite audit and audit controls; full Lean reproduction is a separate documented command. Our reproduction used the upstream local statement comparator, not the official Linux comparator or a second kernel, and is not independent human mathematical review.
